solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Images picked up from one who's had too much of this?

indicators.text: picked up from one who's had too much of
indicators.note: the word is heard as slurred by a drunk speaker, so its sound is thickened into the drink's name

parts.note: snaps are photographs, i.e. images

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a tipsy person mishears pictures, or about what they drank.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk saying SNAPS would slur it to sound like the spirit, and the spirit is what made them drunk: 'this' points back to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark makes 'this' stand for the strong spirit the drunkard has overindulged in.

clue.text: Affluent holding company with excellent trade at first glance

indicators.note: the wealthy word grips the firm's abbreviation in its middle

parts.note: affluent means rich

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the two words that precede it are used

explanation.surface: A wealthy firm with a fine business, as it looks on first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first glance' looks like one idiom, but 'glance' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance off something is to rebound or deflect, as a bullet does when it skips off a surface.

clue.text: Mother's boy that may get in jam

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
a boy is someone's son

explanation.surface: A mother's son who tends to get himself into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a jam' suggests a scrape a boy gets into; here the jam is the preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: This small plum is a classic fruit for making preserves, so it can end up in a pot of jam.

clue.text: Fool's been fleeced of billions — no refund available

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: being stripped or robbed of something takes that letter away from the word

explanation.surface: An idiot has been swindled out of a fortune and cannot get the money back.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold in their current condition carry no guarantee, so the buyer cannot return them for a refund.

clue.text: Head of gendarmerie interrupts naked naughtiness — thus?

definitions.text: Head of gendarmerie interrupts naked naughtiness — thus?

indicators.note: the police letter breaks into the word for unclothed

parts.note: naked means bare

indicators.note: the first letter of the French police word is taken

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing or naughtiness

explanation.surface: A French police chief bursts in on some nude misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the picture: the gendarme, breaking in on the scene, is doing exactly what the answer says.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude abruptly on someone, as the police chief does here, is to burst in uninvited.

clue.text: Try at first to salute quarterdeck?

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words that follow are used

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to greet the officers on the ship's quarterdeck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarterdeck' looks naval; split it as 'quarter deck', a quarter of a pack of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four suits is a quarter of a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: I say so — one's an island

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'
sic is Latin for thus or so
an means one, A

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims and asserts that one thing is an island, echoing 'no man is an island'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean French territory, birthplace of Napoleon, is a large island.

clue.text: Withdraw from euro to revalue what's in circulation

indicators.note: the letters are drawn out of a run spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Advice to pull out of the euro so that the money in use can be revalued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revalue' hints at reversal, but the hidden word reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning part of a machine, something that goes round in circles.

clue.text: Make mild sausage mixes

indicators.note: the letters of the meat word are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe note: sausage mixtures make a mild dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe or ease something, such as pain or anger, is to make it less severe.

clue.text: Mixture of molten rock thrown up around US city

indicators.note: the volcanic word goes round the city letters
in a down entry, thrown upward means read from bottom to top

parts.note: magma is molten rock below the earth's surface
Los Angeles, abbreviated LA, which has to be written backwards here though no clue word says so

explanation.surface: Lava erupting around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's slip: 'thrown up' signals turning only the rock, but Los Angeles must be turned as well for the letters to fit, which the clue never signals.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination of different things.

clue.text: Me, for example? I disagree

definitions.meaning: me (mi) is a tonic sol-fa note but a different one from soh, so it is a note that is not the fifth
a phrase of contradiction, a denial

explanation.surface: Someone offers themselves as an example and is promptly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the third note of the sol-fa scale: a note, but not 'so'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: a note other than soh, and a mild spoken denial.

clue.text: Steed, say, starts to stagger crazily first and totter

indicators.note: these two letters go before the other piece
the opening letters of the next two words are used

parts.note: John Steed is the hero of the British TV series The Avengers, so he is an example of an avenger

explanation.surface: A horse lurches wildly and then wobbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steed' and 'stagger' paint a horse; Steed is the TV spy. A totter is British slang for a rag-and-bone man, who scavenges discarded goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter collects scrap from bins and tips, so he is a forager of others' leftovers.

clue.text: Unusual reproduction showing fowl in chapter of Old Testament book

indicators.note: the bird word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a chapter is a part
O is a short form of of, as in o'clock
a hen is a fowl
Genesis is the first book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A Bible chapter describing a strange birth involving a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' gives O, as in o'clock; 'Old Testament book' is the whole of the last piece, not a source of O.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin birth, development of an egg without fertilisation, is an unusual form of reproduction.

clue.text: Round up sheep to return to groom

indicators.note: the pieces are read back to front

parts.note: to net is to catch or round up
rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: A shepherd gathers the flock and brings it back to be tended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' turns NETRAMS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom oneself is to tidy up one's appearance.

clue.text: A Baltic resident and French/English art lover

parts.note: an Esth is an Estonian, a dated term
et is French for and, and 'and' is implied by the slash

explanation.surface: An Estonian with French and English roots who loves art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French/English' reads as two nationalities but gives the French for 'and' then E.
explanation.definitionFit: An aesthete is a person devoted to beauty and the arts.

clue.text: Liberal briefly confused seeing Clegg outside club

indicators.note: the politician's first name wraps around the jumbled letters

parts.note: Nick Clegg was the UK Liberal Democrat leader

indicators.note: the abbreviated party letters are muddled up

parts.note: LIB is short for Liberal

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg, Liberal Democrat leader, looks bewildered outside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led Britain's Liberal Democrats; 'club' is a golf club, not a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old name for a golf club, roughly a nine iron.

clue.text: Kind of red spy infiltrating America from the east

indicators.note: the spy word gets inside the country letters
in an across entry, reading from the east means right to left

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A Communist spy entering America from the east, a Cold War scenario.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of red' suggests a Communist; it is a colour. 'from the east' turns AM to MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This purplish-red shade is a type of red, named after an 1859 battle.

clue.text: Festival city mainly erected to house third category of stars

indicators.note: the combined pieces enclose the category letter

parts.note: a gala is a festive event

indicators.note: in a down entry, set upright means read bottom to top
most of the word, its last letter dropped

parts.note: the word is used as written before trimming
C is the third grade, after A and B

explanation.surface: A festival city builds a home for third-rate celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' trims CITY to CIT, which 'erected' turns to TIC; GALATIC then 'houses' C, the third class in an A-B-C grading.
explanation.definitionFit: Galactic means relating to a galaxy, a vast system of stars.

clue.text: Leader of team with outward advantage took risks, having a compulsion

parts.note: AD is short for advantage in tennis

indicators.note: the gambling word lies outside the team letter

parts.note: diced, as in diced with death, means gambled or took risks

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A captain with a head start gambled, driven by an urge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outward' puts DICED around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hooked on something means being unable to stop, a compulsive dependence.

clue.text: Thrown out comb with bald side that's hopeless

indicators.note: a hopeless mess of letters is one put in a new order

explanation.surface: A comb thrown out by someone bald, for whom it is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown' looks like part of 'thrown out'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disconcerted or confused is to be thrown, in the sense of knocked off balance.

clue.text: Soft currency? Yen

parts.note: dough is slang for money
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Is the yen a weak currency?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' also means a longing, a further distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something doughy is soft and pliable, like unbaked bread.

clue.text: Drillers involved in despoilment

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the longer word

explanation.surface: Oil companies drilling are implicated in environmental plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers in the petroleum industry drill wells to extract crude.

clue.text: Free from infestation without special instruments

indicators.note: the special letter is removed

parts.note: bugless means without bugs

explanation.surface: Clean of pests apart from some particular tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes S out of BUGLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugles are brass musical instruments used for military calls.

clue.text: Bar bill ending with two zeros

indicators.note: the zeros come at the end

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar
two Os, each looking like a zero

explanation.surface: A pub tab that ends in two noughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub to match 'bill'; it means forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited, so to declare it taboo is to ban it.

clue.text: Increase share in maintenance

parts.note: to up is to increase
a holding is a share in a company

explanation.surface: A rise in someone's portion of the maintenance payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholding something means sustaining or supporting it, i.e. keeping it in place.

clue.text: Solid copper biro

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, like a biro

explanation.surface: A sturdy copper ballpoint pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid' seems to describe the pen; it is a noun for a three-dimensional shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A cube is a solid figure, and cubic describes such a three-dimensional shape.

clue.text: Work peripatetically in the docks, heartlessly exploited

indicators.note: the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
the middle letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Dockers being ruthlessly used, moving from job to job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes C from the middle of DOCKS, leaving DOKS; 'exploited' scrambles THEDOKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot-desking means using whatever desk is free rather than having one's own, so an office worker roams.

clue.text: I will get in record book with typical example

indicators.note: the letter is going to slip inside the other pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Someone vows to get into the record books as a classic case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record book' looks like one phrase, as in the Guinness record books; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect representative of a type, the embodiment of it.
